title: Giant Bicycle Recalls LED-Light Keys Included with SureLock Bike Lock Sets Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violates Mandatory Standard for Consumer Products with Button Cell Batteries
hazard: The LED-light key that was included with certain SureLock Bicycle Lock sets violates the mandatory safety standard for consumer products with button cell and coin batteries because the button batteries can be accessed easily by children, posing an ingestion hazard.  Additionally, the packaging and product do not have the warnings required under Reese's Law. When button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns, and death.
description: This recall involves Giant Bicycle-branded black-and-white LED-light bike lock keys that were included as part of a pre-keyed SureLock bicycle lock set that includes a bike lock and two-or-four keys without an LED-light (depending on the model). Only LED-light bike lock keys manufactured after March 2023 are included in this recall. The list of affected serial numbers is included in the table below. Serial numbers are located on the underside of the bike lock, as shown in the last picture above. remedy: Consumers should stop using the recalled LED-light key that was included with certain SureLock Bicycle Lock sets immediately and contact Giant Bicycle for a $5 refund. Consumers will be asked to bring the LED key to an authorized Giant retailer to participate in the recall and receive the refund. When returning the LED-light key to a retailer, consumers will be required to bring either the complete bicycle lock purchase or a picture of the serial number on the bicycle lock in order to verify the serial number is in the scope of the recall. Consumers may continue to use the bicycle lock and non-LED-light keys included with the SureLock Bicycle Lock sets. Note: Button and Coin cell batteries are hazardous. Batteries should be disposed of or recycled by following local hazardous waste procedures.

title: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.): Tire Repair Kit Bottle Cap May Detach
hazard: A detached bottle cap can become a projectile and strike the user or others nearby, increasing the risk of injury.
description: TIRES Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2023-2026 CR-V Hybrid, Accord Hybrid, and 2025 CR-V Fuel Cell EV vehicles that were previously remedied under NHTSA recall number 26V366. When using the tire repair kit, pressure may build within the sealant bottle, causing the bottle cap to detach.
remedy: Dealers will inspect and replace the tire repair kit nozzle, as necessary, free of charge. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed November 16, 2026. Owners may contact Honda's customer service at 1-866-784-1870. Honda's number for this recall is PPW. Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) involved in this recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning October 17, 2026. Vehicles previously repaired under recall 26V366 will need to have the new remedy completed.

title: Electrical Appliances: Girlanda
hazard: Electric_Shock. The live parts of the lamp cap are accessible when the lamp is partially screwed into the lampholder of the luminaire, leading to electric shock. Consequently, the user could touch accessible live parts and receive an electric shock.
description: LED-lighting chain. AC Mains pluggable with non-detachable power supply cord, class II, 16 A round plug. E27 lamp holders. The product does not comply with the requirements of the Low Voltage Directive and the relevant European standard EN IEC 60598.

title: Machinery: Rechargeable Grass Mower
hazard: Electric_Shock. Due to inadequate insulation between the input and output circuits of the product, the user can receive an electric shock from easily accessible live parts.
description: Electric lithium-ion battery powered lawn mower with attached wall plug. The product does not comply with the requirements of the Machinery Directive.
country: United Kingdom in respect of Northern Ireland

title: Toys: Transport vehicle truck
hazard: Chemical, Choking. The battery compartment screw does not comply with the requirements for battery compartment fasteners because it becomes detached when loosened. As a result, the button batteries inside are easily accessible. A small child may put the batteries in the mouth and swallow them, which could cause choking and/or severe internal injuries to the gastrointestinal tract. The screw or fastener must remain attached to the battery cover or compartment door when loosened or opened.
description: A plastic toy logging truck consisting of an orange cab and a grey cargo bed loaded with imitation wooden logs. The logs are secured to the vehicle with elastic retaining bands. The product does not comply with the requirements of the Toy Safety Directive nor with European standard EN 62115.

title: Electrical Appliances: DM132
hazard: Electric_Shock. The windings in the transformer are not properly fixed or insulated and are too close to the metal parts. Additionally, the safety distances on the printed circuit board are too small and the distance between the live parts and the appliance’s outer casing is insufficient. As a result, accessible parts could become live, increasing the risk of electric shock.
description: White USB wall charger The product does not comply with the requirements of the Low Voltage Directive.
